publication.citation: Russ DE, Patterson-Cross RB, Li L, et al. A harmonized atlas of mouse spinal cord cell types and their spatial organization. Nature Communications 12, 5722 (2021).
publication.license: CC BY 4.0; attribution retained in this derived metadata release.

processedCounts.status: Public processed count matrix and cell/feature metadata are available; they are not bundled in this release.

markerTable.title: Supplementary Table 1: harmonized cell type markers
markerTable.derivation: This release retains the 69 published labels and the first three Wilcoxon-ranked markers per label, not the source XLSX or any cell-level count matrix.

scope.lifeStage: Postnatal harmonized transcriptomic reference; the paper separately validates selected marker panels in adult lumbar tissue.
scope.spatialBoundary: TYPE_LEVEL only. A group label, marker, or adult validation context is not an individual-cell coordinate, atlas registration, or same-cell multimodal join.
scope.knownSourceCaution: The source reports that many mid and ventral clusters have lower robustness; its narrative and Supplementary Table 1 should be reviewed together before a narrow label transfer.

groups.label: Motoneuron and preganglionic
groups.sourceScope: The source names these motor or preganglionic populations; this explorer does not count them as interneuron candidates.

groups.label: CSF-contacting neuron
groups.sourceScope: A distinct CSF-contacting population; not treated here as a project interneuron entity.

groups.label: Dorsal excitatory
groups.sourceScope: Twenty dorsal excitatory populations in the harmonized postnatal reference.

groups.label: Dorsal inhibitory
groups.sourceScope: Fourteen dorsal inhibitory populations in the harmonized postnatal reference.

groups.label: Deep dorsal / mid excitatory
groups.sourceScope: Ten deep-dorsal or mid excitatory populations; the source reports lower robustness for many mid/ventral labels.

groups.label: Deep dorsal / mid inhibitory
groups.sourceScope: Seven deep-dorsal or mid inhibitory populations; source-local taxonomy only.

groups.label: Ventral excitatory
groups.sourceScope: Eight ventral excitatory populations; the source cautions that ventral labels are less robust than dorsal labels.

groups.label: Ventral inhibitory
groups.sourceScope: Six ventral inhibitory populations; source-local taxonomy only.

prototypeCrosswalks.reason: Propriospinal is defined by connection pattern. The Russ taxonomy does not supply a verified project-specific projection edge.
prototypeCrosswalks.notEstablished: A molecular label cannot establish a propriospinal connection or atlas location.

prototypeCrosswalks.reason: The paper discusses possible dI1/dI2/dI3 relationships among a ventral excitatory subset, but does not provide a unique dI3 label for this project entity.
prototypeCrosswalks.notEstablished: No exact dI3 identity, connection, or coordinate is assigned.

prototypeCrosswalks.reason: Vsx2 appears in the retained Supplementary Table 1 marker ranking for Excit-36, but Hoxa10 is not retained as a matching marker and the source does not establish the project SC^Vsx2::Hoxa10 entity.
prototypeCrosswalks.notEstablished: Marker context is not a same-cell identity, caudal segment assignment, or registration.

prototypeCrosswalks.reason: Sim1 appears in the retained Supplementary Table 1 marker ranking for Excit-38. The paper cautions that some ventral marker signals may persist from developmental samples and does not make this an exact project V3 mapping.
prototypeCrosswalks.notEstablished: No exact V3 identity, adult validation, connectivity claim, or coordinate follows.

prototypeCrosswalks.reason: The source discusses V2a-related ventral populations but this crosswalk has no source-pinned cervical, ipsilateral, or project-entity match.
prototypeCrosswalks.notEstablished: A V2a-family relationship is not a cervical ipsilateral circuit assignment or registration.

prototypeCrosswalks.reason: The evidence entity is a transmitter-state overlay. It may be compared with inhibitory taxonomy groups but is not a single Russ population.
prototypeCrosswalks.notEstablished: No KCC2 state, injury effect, or causal intervention is inferred from the taxonomy.

prototypeCrosswalks.reason: The evidence entity describes a condition-dependent transmitter-state overlay, not a stable single-population label.
prototypeCrosswalks.notEstablished: Taxonomy does not prove switching, injury state, or cell-level longitudinal identity.

hardBoundaries: All 69 records are type-level molecular metadata, not a census of every interneuron.
No population, marker, crosswalk, or adult-validation statement creates REG, an xyz coordinate, a morphology link, or a synaptic edge.
The crosswalk never upgrades a prototype entity to OBS; current entity glyphs remain SYN and paths remain SCH.
Ambiguous, broad, and marker-context relationships remain explicit; no entity receives an exact Russ mapping in this release.
